item.title: 'He said pistol was unloaded': Injured staff on Varanasi airport firing incident
item.description: Two cargo screeners were injured when a passenger's pistol accidentally discharged during security checks. The passenger claimed the weapon was unloaded before he pressed the trigger to show them. One screener sustained an injury to his left hand, while the other was hit in both legs. The incident occurred at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport while boarding a flight to Mumbai.
item.dc:creator: TOI CITY DESK

item.title: CM Vijay condemns killing of 3 Tamil farmers in Karnataka; Stalin seeks judicial probe
item.description: Political leaders across Tamil Nadu have expressed outrage over the tragic killing of three farmers by Karnataka forest officials. Former Chief Minister M K Stalin has called for a judicial inquiry and demanded compensation for the bereaved families. He has also asked the Tamil Nadu government to publicly denounce Karnataka's actions.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement hint, reveals plans for life after football
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has suggested the 2026-27 season could be the final year of his playing career, saying he wants to leave a “spectacular legacy”. The 41-year-old remains contracted to Al Nassr until June 2027 and has begun planning life after football, including spending more time with family, travelling and playing padel.

item.title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
item.description: MacKenzie Scott's donations have enabled medical debt abolition across America. Her model allows acquiring debt at low costs and then forgiving it. This approach has inspired other billionaires to contribute millions to similar causes. While philanthropic efforts are scaling, policy reforms for medical debt remain stalled. Scott's work highlights immediate relief possibilities and the need for systemic change.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Exam-conducting body NTA admits errors, orders fresh NET test for 3 subjects
item.description: National Testing Agency acknowledged extensive errors in UGC-NET English, Commerce, and Sociology papers. Fresh examinations for these three subjects have been ordered by the agency. These re-tests are scheduled to take place on September 9 and 10. The decision came after multiple complaints regarding factual and typographical errors were received. Results for the other 84 subjects will be declared as scheduled.

item.title: US immigration authority: These forms will be rejected from September 15
item.description: USCIS will introduce new editions of immigration forms I-539 and I-765. These revised forms will be effective starting September 15, 2026. Applications submitted using older forms after this date will be rejected. This change aligns with a recently published immigration rule. USCIS emphasizes there will be no grace period for this form update.

item.title: Invasive carp make up 90% of fish killed in Mississippi River
item.description: Hundreds of dead fish have washed up along the Mississippi River in Missouri and Illinois, but wildlife officials say the die-off may benefit the ecosystem. About 90% of the fish found at one Missouri site were invasive silver and bighead carp. Warm temperatures, low water levels and reduced oxygen appear to have caused the deaths.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Ryanair co-founder’s $14M Kentucky horse farm now listed for $57.5M
item.description: Ryanair co-founder Tony Ryan bought Kentucky’s historic Castleton Farm for $14 million in 2001. Now, his family is seeking $57.5 million for the 951-acre estate, which includes a 13,500-square-foot Greek Revival mansion, 16 barns, 268 stalls, 10 homes and historic landmarks. The property, once home to celebrated racehorses, heads to auction October 28.

item.title: Elon Musk makes a promise to employees at townhall
item.description: SpaceX aims to enhance its AI model Grok by integrating insights from its workforce. Elon Musk envisions this initiative as a means to embed human values deeply into the AI's framework. Employees are not only invited to enhance the internal AI systems but are also inspired to share their expertise.

item.title: From burnt cash to possibly first impeachment: Justice Varma saga explained
item.description: Justice Yashwant Varma's residence was engulfed in flames, leading to the shocking discovery of burnt currency notes. A subsequent parliamentary inquiry confirmed serious charges against him, prompting his resignation. The Centre's pursuit of impeachment aims to set a strong precedential framework for judicial accountability. This case also poses critical questions about the interplay between a judge's resignation and ongoing disciplinary proceedings, potentially impacting future cases of judicial misconduct.
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: Brittany Mahomes explains why female athletes deserve more recognition
item.description: Brittany Mahomes has made her support for women’s sports clear while celebrating the launch of KC Current Studios. The former soccer player and Kansas City Current co-owner emphasized the impact sports can have beyond competition, including confidence, friendship and inspiration for young people. Her comments come amid wider debates surrounding women’s sports, though she focused on celebrating female athletes and ensuring their stories receive greater attention and recognition.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: How fatherhood and his daughters changed Dak Prescott’s outlook on life
item.description: Dak Prescott’s journey into fatherhood has transformed how he views life, time and legacy. The Dallas Cowboys quarterback now looks beyond football and wants to experience every stage of his children’s lives, including seeing the families they may build someday. His perspective reflects the powerful impact of becoming a parent, especially after losing his own mother. For Prescott, success is no longer measured only by achievements, but by being present for family.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Why NHL players tape their sticks and how it improves puck control
item.description: NHL players tape their sticks for reasons that go way beyond hockey tradition. The tape changes the feel of the blade on the puck, helps prevent ice buildup, protects equipment and gives players a customized grip. From Connor McDavid to other NHL stars, individual tape jobs can be a reflection of playing style, comfort, visual preference, and well-established pregame routines.

item.title: ‘Rankings don’t matter’: Pakistan captain’s bold India warning ahead of WC clash
item.description: Captain Abu Bakar Mahmood of Pakistan dismisses the importance of rankings as his team gears up for the high-stakes match against India. He believes that the actual performance will determine the winner on the field. After ten years without a win against their fiercest opponents, Pakistan are eager to advance to the World Cup quarterfinals, relying on a blend of youthful energy and seasoned leadership to reclaim their legacy.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: What happened to MLB legend Tommy John? Baseball icon dies at 83 after 26-year career
item.description: What happened to Tommy John? The MLB legend died peacefully at 83 at his Florida home, surrounded by his family. Days earlier, he had been in hospice care and shared a farewell message with Yankees fans. John finished his 26-year career with 288 wins, but his greatest legacy came from returning to baseball after groundbreaking elbow surgery.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Gaza peace plan: 8 nations condemn Israel's rejection of US roadmap
item.description: Several nations condemned Israel's rejection of the Gaza peace process proposal. This move seriously undermines collective efforts to achieve lasting peace and stability. The roadmap, accepted by Palestinian factions, was a culmination of intensive mediation efforts. Israel insists Hamas must be disarmed before any troop withdrawal occurs. The countries urged the US to compel Israel to fully comply with the plan.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: ‘Clearly, there’s something wrong’: Gavaskar questions India’s fitness methods
item.description: Sunil Gavaskar, the legendary former captain, raises concerns regarding the fitness and training methodologies of the Indian cricket team. He points out that the spate of hamstring injuries suggests flaws in the existing training strategies. Furthermore, Gavaskar questions the rationale behind limiting bowlers' net sessions in the name of biomechanics, insisting that match fitness should take priority over purely gym-focused conditioning.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: 'Stay away from politics': TMC leader Asish Banerjee's suicide note surfaces
item.description: Former Trinamool Congress MLA Asish Banerjee was found dead at his party office. A suicide note was discovered, which reportedly mentioned his political journey. Banerjee had served as a five-time MLA and held ministerial portfolios. He stepped down from a party committee after losing his seat. His body was taken for a post-mortem examination.

item.title: Arsenal’s Calafiori sets 118-year record with fastest-ever Community Shield goal
item.description: Riccardo Calafiori scored after just 23 seconds against Manchester City to give Arsenal a record-breaking start in the 2026 Community Shield. His strike became the fastest goal in the competition’s 118-year history, beating Liverpool legend Gary McAllister’s previous Cardiff record. Arsenal then doubled their advantage through Kai Havertz, giving Mikel Arteta’s side an impressive opening to the season.

item.title: ‘Rahul, Hemant are dead’: Jharkhand protester performs ‘funeral’, shaves head
item.description: The protest by students and job aspirants over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations entered its 23rd day on Sunday, with the protesters, under the banner of JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, accusing the ruling JMM-Congress alliance of failing to take “concrete action” on their demands. They have also announced plans to gherao Soren's residence in Ranchi on August 20 and demanded his resignation.
item.dc:creator: TOI NEWS DESK

item.title: IND vs SL: The ninety minutes! Moving day comes early in gloomy Galle
item.description: A rain-hit Day 2 in Galle turned into a frantic 90 minutes as Sri Lanka's bowlers struck in quick succession, dismissing India's overnight batters and bringing the hosts back into the contest. Devdutt Padikkal's 167 and a crucial lower-order stand kept India in control, but the pitch is beginning to offer the turn and bounce expected in Galle.
item.dc:creator: SAHIL MALHOTRA

item.title: Rs 6,400-crore IPO rush: 7 companies set to tap primary market next week
item.description: The IPO market anticipates a busy week with seven companies planning public offerings. These upcoming issues aim to collectively raise more than Rs 6,400 crore from investors. Horizon Industrial Parks and Lalithaa Jewellery Mart will launch their initial public offerings on August 17. Shankesh Jewellers and Sunshine Pictures are scheduled to open their issues on August 18.

item.title: ‘Unwanted record’: Ex-captain stunned after bizarre blunder by Pak at World Cup
item.description: Pakistan's hockey captain received a green card after gear was forgotten. This incident occurred during their opening World Cup match against England. The team failed to produce necessary protective equipment for a penalty corner. Former captain Salman Akbar criticised the lack of preparation and organisation. This lapse raises serious questions about the team's readiness for major events.

item.title: Beyond bloodline: How donated milk is saving India’s most vulnerable newborns
item.description: Human milk banks in India serve a critical purpose by delivering much-needed nourishment to at-risk infants. Generous lactating mothers donate their surplus milk, helping those newborns who can’t receive it from their biological mothers. Every donation undergoes thorough screening and pasteurisation to ensure safety, highlighting the significant impact these banks have on the health of premature and sick children.

item.title: A flat headache: Why England flats have no takers despite price cuts
item.description: In the current market, English flat owners are facing significant challenges in selling their properties, with many listings lingering for months. Frequent price reductions and failed deals lead to decreasing valuations, while leasehold issues and mismatched price expectations between buyers and investors create additional obstacles. The tightening of mortgage lending conditions and surveyor downvaluations complicate the situation further, leaving small landlords grappling with unsold properties and growing complexities.

item.title: Punjab Police foils terror plot, recovers 690 gram IED
item.description: Amritsar Rural Police have effectively disrupted a potential terrorist attack aimed at a police establishment, recovering a 690-gram improvised explosive device. The Bomb Disposal Squad swiftly defused the explosive, ensuring public safety. In light of Independence Day approaching, security measures have been ramped up, and a case is currently under investigation to unravel further details.

item.title: Hockey World Cup: India hold Olympic silver medallists China to 2-2 draw
item.description: India kicked off their Hockey World Cup journey with a challenging 2-2 draw against China. Navneet Kaur opened the scoring, putting India ahead early on. However, Zhang Ying equalised with a penalty stroke. Deepika regained the lead for India with a penalty corner in the second quarter, only for Ma Ning to score in the third and equalise again.

item.title: ‘Going to go back to bed now’: Padikkal after career-best 167 in Galle Test
item.description: Devdutt Padikkal smashed his maiden Test century, converting his overnight 131 into a career-best 167 against Sri Lanka in Galle. The left-hander credited two years of hard work, clear plans against spin and confident footwork for his breakthrough. Padikkal also stressed staying focused after reaching 100, helping India reach a strong 460/9.
